items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the tax law, in relation to providing banking corporations with a tax credit for investment in certified bank capital companies
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4310

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the tax law, in relation to providing banking corporations with
a tax credit for investment in certified bank capital companies

PURPOSE:
To provide banking corporations with incentives to create a pool of
venture capital funds, managed by venture capital professionals, for
investment in small, New York based firms.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:
§ 1- Statement of legislative intent.

§ 2- Amends § 1456 of the Tax Law by adding a new subsection (x). The
new subsection permits a taxpayer (defined in section 1452(a) as a
banking corporation) to take a tax credit equal to one hundred
percent of an investment made in a Certified Bank Capital Company
(BANCAPCO), at a rate of ten percent a year. If a BANCAPCO is
decertified for not complying with the requirements of the bill, some
or all of the credits can be recaptured. Tax credits earned through
an investment in a Certified Bank Capital Company are not subject to
a retaliatory tax which would otherwise be imposed as a result of
obtaining the credit.

§ 3- Amends the Tax Law by adding a new § 35.  This section
establishes the
requirements for a venture capital firm to be certified by the state
for the purpose of receiving investments from certified Investors,
defined as banking corporations. It defines the types of businesses
qualified to receive venture capital investments from BANCAPCOs based
on size (fewer than 100 employees) or annual gross ($5 million, but
not to exceed 200 employees). No more than 14% of BANCAPCOs funds may
be invested in anyone company. The bill sets the amount of certified
capital that is eligible for tax credits at $50 million for calendar
year 2008, and $100 million thereafter.

Businesses receiving BANCAPCO funds are required to state their
intention to conduct their business operations in New York State. In
addition, BANCAPCOs are required to maintain at least 90% of their
investment portfolios in in-state firms despite any relocations of
businesses that might occur. If firm relocations occur which bring a
BANCAPCO's portfolio below that level, the BANCAPCO is required to
make a compensating investment in an in-state company of equal amount
to that invested in the relocated firm.

To ensure diversity and increase the likelihood that several venture
capital funds will be established, the bill limits the amount that
any certified investor can invest to $10 million in anyone year in
which such an investment can be made. Therefore, no one investor can
invest more than $20 million of the authorized $100 million. However,
if the total amount authorized has not been invested 60 days prior to
the end of each year, the limitation ceases to be in effect so that
the total amount can be invested. Affiliated banking companies are
considered to be one taxpayer and investor.


A BANCAPCO must invest its certified funds in qualified businesses at
a specific rate (25% within 2 years, 40% within 3 years, and 50%
within 5 years). Before a BANCAPCO can make a distribution to its
equity holders, it must invest 100% of its certified capital. If a
BANCAPCO fails to meet specified requirements, it can be decertified,
and some or all of the tax credits available to its investors can be
recaptured and/or revoked, depending at what point in time
decertification occurs.

Each BANCAPCO is required to provide to the Department of Taxation and
Finance an audited financial statement annually, which must include
the opinion of an independent certified public accountant. The
Department is charged with conducting an annual review of the
BANCAPCOs to determine if they are abiding by the requirements of the
statute.

An applicant seeking to become a BANCAPCO is charged a fee of $500 to
file an application with the Department. It is also charged an annual
certification fee of $500.
The department is required to promulgate rules and regulations within
120 days of implementation of this act.

§ 4- Effective Date.

JUSTIFICATION:
New York State has not attracted an amount of national venture capital
commitments commensurate with its economic size. Venture investments
continue to be concentrated in California and Massachusetts.
California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Texas, and Washington are the
only states that have finished in the top ten in attracting venture
investments in each of the past five years.

In 1997-1998, New York State developed a new vehicle, the Certified
Capital Company, to provide insurance companies the incentives for
the creation of state venture capital
funds directed to the formation of new, and expansion of existing,
businesses which create jobs, with an emphasis on the smaller,
earlier-stage deals that have difficulty in attracting institutional
venture capital. The creation of a Certified Bank Capital Company to
provide banking corporations the incentive for the creation of
another state venture capital fund in New York can further help to
fill the venture capital gap that currently exists in the State and
promote economic development.

From a "present value" basis (using the prime rate of interest for
discounting), because investors must invest all of their money up
front, while credits are earned over a ten year period, the BANCAPCO
credit is closer to 65% of the funds invested, not 100%.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:
2009-2010: A.2817
2007-2008: A.4548/S.4683
2005-2006: A.3669-A/S.4037-A
2003-2004: A.3400/S.2614
2001-2002: A.950/S.3741
1999-2000: A.6628/S.5387


FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:
FY: 2010-2011 - None
FY: 2011-2012 - $5 Million
FY: 2012-2013 - $10 Million

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Provides a tax credit for certain investments in certified bank capital companies to provide venture capital for small business enterprises which have traditionally experienced difficulty in attracting institutional venture capital; creates a full framework for implementation.
title: Provides a tax credit for certain investments in certified bank capital companies to provide venture capital for certain small business enterprises
